Malaysia Imposes Tariffs on Imported Solar Panels, Shaking Renewable Energy Industry

KUALA LUMPUR – The Malaysian government has imposed new tariffs on imported solar panels and related components, a move that is reverberating across the country’s renewable energy industry. Announced last week by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry, the tariffs—set at 30%—took effect on Monday and apply to all imported photovoltaic modules and inverters.

Officials stated that the measure aims to “bolster domestic manufacturing capacity and support local innovation.” However, the immediate effects on domestic renewable energy firms have been significant. Many companies, including major solar installation and development groups, have reported delays in project timelines as they scramble to adjust procurement strategies.

“We are currently reviewing our supply chain and project budgets in light of the new tariffs,” said Lim Wei Jun, Chief Operating Officer of SunArc Energy, a major Malaysian solar developer. “While we welcome efforts to strengthen local manufacturing, the sudden cost increases are impacting ongoing and planned installations.”

Industry analysts estimate that the tariffs could raise total project costs by 8–12% in the short term. Some firms with existing inventories of imported panels are temporarily insulated, but most are warning of potential slowdowns.

“The biggest concern is for workers at project sites,” said Nurul Huda, spokesperson for the Malaysia Renewable Workforce Alliance. “Several contractors are already reporting reduced hours, and there is anxiety about future layoffs if project pipelines shrink.”

According to the Malaysian Renewable Energy Association, approximately 13,000 jobs are directly tied to the industry’s development and installation sectors. The group has called for urgent consultations with the government to address concerns about market stability and employment.

As the tariffs remain in force, stakeholders across the renewable energy industry are closely watching for further clarifications on the policy’s duration and potential relief measures.
